Scale for rm. The paper's own running example: for rm, Caruca generates 8,749,056 invocation configurations, pairing each invocation with file-system states (path missing, a file,
an empty or non-empty directory) so that pre- and post-conditions can be read off what changed. The agent ran rm 27 times, on files and folders it created itself.
v1 is shown as the paper designs it (sections 2-6), not as run for this comparison. The rm sample's syntax file is v1's curated reference (syntax_specs/rm.py). Method, not quality, is compared here.
